elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: New Section 5.4 as rendered: "Termination for Convenience by IBM. IBM may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to MSL..." The element is disjunctive (Agreement or Order Form), so Agreement-level coverage suffices; the retained SOW 6.1 Purchase Order cancellation right is untouched and does not conflict.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to MSL" — exactly 30 days, in writing, and no additional conditions or consents attached.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "MSL shall refund to IBM, pro rata, any fees prepaid by IBM for the period after the effective date of termination." Pro-rata basis is express, not merely inferred from a post-termination period.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Section 4.0 fixes a three-year initial term "unless terminated as provided in Section 5.0", and Section 5.1 opens "this Agreement may be terminated by either Party for cause as follows" — the only mid-term exits enumerated are cause-based. The six (6) months' notice in Section 4.0 operates on the automatic twelve-month renewal (natural-term non-renewal), which the playbook routes to RENEWAL rather than T4C. No new MSL convenience right is created by the insertion.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted clause uses thirty (30) days' notice, which is outside the 60–90 day fallback band (and is Customer-favourable). Fallback level is therefore incomplete, but this is immaterial because the preferred level is complete.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the insertion imposes no early-termination fee or penalty on IBM for a convenience exit, and no retained clause attaches a termination charge to Agreement-level convenience termination (SOW 6.1 cost reimbursement is Purchase-Order specific and pre-existing).

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Condition effectively does not apply: Section 5.1 limits MSL termination to cause, so MSL has no convenience right at all mid-term; its only notice-based exit is the Section 4.0 non-renewal operating at the end of the then-current renewal period.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply — MSL holds no convenience termination right; the only MSL notice mechanic (Section 4.0 non-renewal) requires six (6) months, which exceeds 90 days in any event.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all four preferred elements are met on the operative text — a 30-day IBM convenience right, express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and a retained for-cause-only regime that leaves MSL with no mid-term convenience exit.

The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present" returned false, but inspection of the rendered operative language shows the express clause "IBM may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to MSL"; the regex result appears to reflect the pre-redline baseline (consistent with the 'missing' finding) and does not undercut substantive coverage. Element coverage and minimality gates both pass.

Minimality holds: the insertion is a single concise sentence, drops the model language's surplus "or any Order Form, in whole or in part" (correctly, since no Order Form/partial-termination structure is required by the selected checklist), adds no survival tail, expense allocation, procedure, or extra remedy, and no words are deleted from Sections 4.0, 5.0, SOW 6.1 or the Parts pricing paragraph.

Intent preserved: the new right is placed inside Section 5.0, so Section 4.0's "unless terminated as provided in Section 5.0" cross-reference remains intact; the Section 5.1 "notwithstanding" sentence is a grant of for-cause rights rather than an exclusivity bar, so it does not contradict the new subsection; the six-month non-renewal mechanic, the Purchase Order cancellation/cost-reimbursement allocation, and the Parts pricing formula all survive unchanged.

Drafting nit (not a failure): "fees" is lower-case ordinary language and not a defined term in this manufacturing agreement, which uses "Price"; consider conforming to "amounts prepaid by IBM" or "prepaid Price" to avoid an argument that no 'fees' are prepaid, and confirm whether MSL will seek to attach the SOW 6.1-style cost reimbursement to an Agreement-level convenience exit.

Fallback is not independently satisfied only because notice is 30 days rather than 60–90; no repair is required since the preferred checklist is complete, and the comment correctly offers 60–90 days as the concession path.
